facts.statement: A 2016 study estimated Lophostropheus could reach 5.2 meters in length and weigh 136 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2016 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi gave a higher estimation of 5.2 meters (17 ft) and 136 kg (300 lbs).

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is classified within the theropod superfamily Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: It has been assigned to the superfamily Coelophysoidea.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is distinguished by prominent crests on its neck vertebrae and an extra pair of cavities in those vertebrae, features not found in Liliensternus.
facts.quote: It also has prominent crests on the tops and bottoms of its neck vertebrae (for which it was named), and an extra pair of cavities in its neck vertebrae, unlike Liliensternus.

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Lophostropheus were found in 2024 in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, marking the first dinosaur remains discovered in that region.
facts.quote: Teeth found after a landslide on the German river Prüm in 2024 are thought to belong to a Lophostropheus and are among the first dinosaur remains ever found in Rhineland-Palatinate.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis placed Lophostropheus phylogenetically close to the derived theropods Sinosaurus and Cryolophosaurus.
facts.quote: An analysis of early dinosaurs by Baron, Norman and Barrett (2017) placed Lophostropheus in a position close to the derived theropods Sinosaurus and Cryolophosaurus.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus fossils were found in the Moon-Airel Formation in Normandy, France.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Moon-Airel de Normandía, Francia.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton from the Triassic-Jurassic boundary in Normandy was originally described in 1966 as Halticosaurus sp.
facts.quote: En 1966, los paleontólogos franceses C. Larsonneur y Albert-Félix de Lapparent describieron un esqueleto parcial del límite Triásico-Jurásico de Normandía como Halticosaurus sp.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen at the University of Caen includes a tooth, five cervical vertebrae, two dorsal vertebrae, four sacral vertebrae, tail vertebrae, portions of all pelvic bones, and an unidentified fragment.
facts.quote: Este espécimen, hoy en la Universidad de Caen, consiste en un diente, cinco vértebras del cuello, dos vértebras de la espalda, cuatro vértebras sacras, vértebras de la cola, porciones de todos los huesos pélvicos, y un fragmento no identificado.

facts.statement: In 1993, Gilles Cuny and Peter Galton reinterpreted the specimen as a new species of Liliensternus named L. airelensis.
facts.quote: Este fue reinterpretado en 1993 por Gilles Cuny y Peter Galton como una nueva especie de Liliensternus a la que llamaron L. airelensis.

facts.statement: Researchers noted differences between L. airelensis and the type species L. liliensterni, leading Ezcurra and Cuny to assign it to the new genus Lophostropheus in 2007.
facts.quote: Otros investigadores notaron diferencias entre L. airelensis y la especie tipo L. liliensterni, hasta que en 2007, Martin Ezcurra y Cuny lo asignaron a su propio género, Lophostropheus.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected in 1959 from sediments deposited at the Rhaetian-Hettangian boundary, approximately 201 to 200 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue recogido por Pareyn en 1959 en piedra arcillosa arenosa y lenticular, caliza arenosa que se depositó en el límite del Rhaetiense a finales del Triásico y el Hettangiense de principios del Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 201-200 millones de años.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is one of the few dinosaurs known to have lived during the Triassic-Jurassic boundary.
facts.quote: Es uno de los pocos dinosaurios que se sabe que vivió durante el límite Triásico-Jurásico.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is one of the few dinosaurs that may have survived the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event, when at least half of known species went extinct.
facts.quote: Lophostropheus es uno de los pocos dinosaurios que pudo haber sobrevivido al evento de extinción Triásico-Jurásico cuando al menos la mitad de las especies conocidas que viven en la Tierra se extinguieron.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is more closely related to coelophysids, including Coelophysis, than to Liliensternus.
facts.quote: Es más cercano a los celofísidos, incluyendo el bien conocido Coelophysis, que a Liliensternus.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is included in a clade that excludes Coelophysis and Zupaysaurus.
facts.quote: De hecho, es incluido en un clado sin Coelophysis y Zupaysaurus.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus possesses derived theropod features such as a spherical joint at the front of neck and tail vertebrae and a vertical ridge on the ilium.
facts.quote: Tiene características similares de otros terópodos derivados, como la articulación esférica en la parte delantera de las vértebras del cuello y las de la cola, y un reborde vertical en el ilion.

facts.statement: The animal has prominent crests above and below the neck vertebrae, which inspired its scientific name, and an extra pair of cavities in these vertebrae compared to Liliensternus.
facts.quote: También tiene crestas prominentes sobre y bajo las vértebras del cuello, que motivaron su nombre científico, y un par extra de cavidades en estas mismas vértebras, a diferencia de Liliensternus.

facts.statement: Lophostropheus lived from the Rhaetian to the Hettangian, between 205.7 and 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Hettangian (205.7 to 199.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Lophostropheus belongs to the parent group Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: Lophostropheus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
